osmTags.inscription: Laus deo to the memory of the men of Hertford who gave their lives in the Great War 1914-1919 also in the 2nd World War 1939-1945. Their name liveth for evermore
John Briant 1748-1829, noted bell founder and clock maker, cast over 100 bells on this site
The Green Dragon Inn was on this site from at least 1620. Rebuilt in 1903 as one of the first hotels to cater for motorists
RT Andrews (1838-1928) & WF Andrews (1839-1918), antiquarians, local benefactors and founders of Hertford Museum, lived here
Yeomanry House, built c1725, is considered to be one of Hertford's finest houses. It has been used by the army since c1910
C15th house, with C17th & C19th alterations. Old Cross Post Office was sited here 1899-2003
Home of the Hertfordshire Mercury 1854-2003, established as the Hartford Mercury by Stephen Austin in 1772
Annie Shepherd Swan (Mrs Burnett Smith) 1859-1943, novelist, lived in this house 1908-1912
In this house lived Alfred Russel Wallace OM. LLD. DCL. FRS. FLS born 1823 - died 1913 naturalist author scientist educated at Hertford Grammar School

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
